senses.gloss: ch. same, to see, recognize, to decide.
units: <cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 29:10">Targ. O. Gen. XXIX, 10</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Berakhot 45a:2">Ber. 45ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Eruvin 14b:20">Erub. 14ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>פוק חֲזִי וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="D00076"><he>דְּבַר</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Eruvin 13b:5">Ib. 13ᵇ</cite> <he>דחֲזִיתֵיה לר״מ וכ׳</he> (not <he>דחזיתא</he>) because I have seen R. M. &c.

Ḥull. 59ᵇ בעינא דאֶיחְזֵי וכ׳ I want to see your God Erub. 63ᵃ ח׳ לנפשיה may examine the knife for his own use; a. fr.—Part. pass. חָזֵי, חֲזֵי, f. חַזְיָא (cmp. רָאוּי) pointed out, fit for, prepared; (it is) proper.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 15:11">Targ. Job XV, 11</cite>.
<cite ref="Onkelos Leviticus 5:10">Targ. O. Lev. V, 10</cite>; a. e.—
<cite ref="Ketubot 21a">Keth. 21ᵃ</cite> <he>כְּדַחֲ׳</he>, <he>כִּדְחָ׳</he> as it is proper.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 19b:12">B. Bath. 19ᵇ</cite> <he>ח׳ לבהמתו</he> fit for his cattle as feed; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Shabbat 90a:8">Sabb. 90ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>למאי חזיא</he> what is it good for (what use can be made of it)?—Pl. <cite ref="H00505"><he>חָזוּ</he></cite>, <cite ref="H00505"><he>חֲזוּ</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Shabbat 90a:8">Ib.</cite> top <he>ח׳ למתק וכ׳</he> they may be used for seasoning &c.
Bets. 26ᵇ; a. fr.—חזי לי it was pointed out to me, I saw.
<cite ref="Gittin 57a:13">Gitt. 57ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Taanit 25b:9">Taan. 25ᵇ</cite>; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to show, let see, reveal; to lay before a teacher for examination or decision.
units: <cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 41:28">Targ. O. Gen. XLI, 28</cite>; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Chullin 59b:9">Ḥull. 59ᵇ</cite> <he>בעינא דמַחֲזִית וכ׳</he> I want thee to show it to me. Bets. l. c. <he>אַחֲזַיֵיה לחכם וכ׳</he> as soon as he showed it to an expert (and the latter decided favorably) &c.; a. fr.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 67a:1">B. Mets. 67ᵃ</cite> <he>ואודיק חַזִּיתָן איילונית</he> and when he looked at me (and noticed that I was going to object by referring to <cite ref="A00722"><he>אוֹנָאָה</he></cite>), he pointed out to us the case of <cite ref="A01283"><he>אַיְילוֹנִית</he></cite> (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 50; Ms. R. <cite ref="H00568"><he>חַזְּתָן</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Judges 13:10">Targ. Jud. XIII, 10</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Berakhot 17b:9">Ber. 17ᵇ</cite> <he>מִיחֲזֵי כיוהרא</he> it looks like assumption; a. fr.
<cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 42:1">Targ. O. Gen. XLII, 1</cite>.
<cite ref="Beitzah 26b:20">Bets. 26ᵇ</cite> <he>אי דאִחֲזוּ בה״ש א׳</he> if on the entrance of the Sabbath they became fit for use, they have become so (for the entire Sabbath).
<cite ref="Beitzah 26b:20">Ib.</cite> <he>אחזו והדר … אחזו</he> they had been fit (on the entrance of the Sabbath), and were unfitted (through rain), and became fit again; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to be shown, to be laid before the scholar for decision. Ib. אתח׳ לחכם וכ׳ it had been shown to (and decided upon by) the expert on the eve &c.; a. fr.
